newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Perot Systems buys Swissair's Icarus.
newsitem.headline: Perot Systems buys Swissair's Icarus.

text.p: U.S. company Perot Systems Corp. will take over Icarus Consulting AG, a management consulting group 55 percent owned by Swissair AG, Swissair said.
Perot, a leading information group, will take over 70 percent of Icarus' capital immediately and the remaining 30 percent will gradually be acquired over the next three years.
Icarus' management owned 45 percent of the company.
During the same time frame, Icarus' workforce of 32 will roughly be tripled.
Icarus has specialised in advising tourism and transport companies, such as airlines, freight forwarders, hotels or railways.
A Swissair spokesman declined to comment on a sales price for its Icarus stake.
Both of Icarus' managing directors, Ludwig Bertsch and Rainer Behrendt will be working under James Champy, Perot's chairman of consulting.
Dallas-based Perot has annual sales of $600 million and personnel of over 4,600 worldwide.
In early 1996 Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) and Perot agreed on a strategic alliance under which Perot handles SBC's non-banking specific information technology issues.
Perot received a 40 percent stake in SBC's Systor AG unit which handles systems integration for banking technology.
SBC gave Perot annually contracts worth $250 million and transferred 800 of its own information technology people to Perot.
For this SBC received the right to acquire 10 million of Perot's shares over a period of about 10 years.
